issues.description: SQL injection vulnerability in searchTodos(). User-supplied keyword is directly interpolated into SQL query using template literals without any sanitization or parameterization. An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL by passing malicious input like `'; DROP TABLE todos; --`.
issues.suggestion: Use parameterized query with LIKE wildcards: const query = 'SELECT * FROM todos WHERE title LIKE $1 OR description LIKE $2'; const pattern = `%${keyword}%`; const rows = await db.query(query, [pattern, pattern]);

issues.description: SQL injection vulnerability in searchTodosByStatus(). User input 'completed' is concatenated directly into SQL query using string concatenation. An attacker can pass malicious SQL like `1 OR 1=1; DROP TABLE todos; --` to execute arbitrary SQL commands.
issues.suggestion: Use parameterized query and validate input type: Ensure 'completed' is a boolean, then use: const query = 'SELECT * FROM todos WHERE completed = $1'; await db.query(query, [completed]);

issues.description: SQL injection vulnerability in getTodosByUser(). The userId parameter is interpolated into SQL query using template literals without sanitization. An attacker can inject SQL by passing userId like `' OR '1'='1` to bypass authorization or exfiltrate data from other users.
issues.suggestion: Use parameterized query: const query = 'SELECT t.* FROM todos t JOIN user_todos ut ON t.id = ut.todo_id WHERE ut.user_id = $1'; const rows = await db.query(query, [userId]);

issues.description: Weak ID generation using Math.random(). This produces predictable IDs that an attacker could guess, potentially allowing unauthorized access to todos. Math.random() is not cryptographically secure and Date.now() is highly predictable.
issues.suggestion: Use cryptographically secure random generation: import { randomUUID } from 'crypto'; function generateId(): string { return randomUUID(); } // Or use crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('hex')

issues.description: Missing type definition and error handling for database module. The './database' import has no type checking, which could lead to runtime errors if db.query doesn't exist or has a different signature than expected.
issues.suggestion: Create a typed database interface: interface Database { query(sql: string, params?: any[]): Promise<any[]>; } export const db: Database; This ensures type safety and catches mismatches at compile time.

issues.description: Incomplete XSS sanitization. The sanitizeInput function only handles HTML entity encoding but doesn't prevent all XSS vectors. It's also being applied to data stored in the database rather than at output time, which violates the principle of storing raw data and sanitizing on output.
issues.suggestion: Remove sanitization before storage and sanitize at output time based on context. For HTML output, use a robust library like DOMPurify or a templating engine with auto-escaping. Store raw data: const todo = { title: input.title.trim(), description: input.description || '' };

issues.description: No error handling for database operations in createTodo(). If db.query() fails (e.g., connection error, constraint violation), the error will propagate without context, making debugging difficult and potentially leaking database internals to clients.
issues.suggestion: Add try-catch with appropriate error handling: try { await db.query(query, params); } catch (error) { throw new Error('Failed to create todo: ' + (error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error')); }

issues.description: getAllTodos() has no pagination, which could cause performance issues and memory exhaustion when the todos table grows large. Loading all records into memory is a potential DoS vector.
issues.suggestion: Add pagination parameters: export async function getAllTodos(limit: number = 100, offset: number = 0): Promise<Todo[]> { const query = 'SELECT * FROM todos ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT $1 OFFSET $2'; const rows = await db.query(query, [limit, offset]); return rows as Todo[]; }

issues.description: Unsafe type assertion 'as Todo[]' without runtime validation. If the database schema changes or returns unexpected data, this will cause runtime type mismatches that TypeScript cannot catch.
issues.suggestion: Add runtime validation using a library like zod or io-ts: import { z } from 'zod'; const TodoSchema = z.object({ id: z.string(), title: z.string(), description: z.string(), completed: z.boolean(), createdAt: z.date() }); return TodoSchema.array().parse(rows);

issues.description: Same unsafe type assertion 'as Todo' without validation. Database could return null values or unexpected types that violate the Todo interface.
issues.suggestion: Validate the result before returning: if (rows.length === 0) return null; const result = rows[0]; if (!result.id || !result.title) { throw new Error('Invalid todo data from database'); } return result as Todo;

issues.description: updateTodoStatus() doesn't verify that the todo exists before updating, returning success even if no rows were affected. This could mask bugs where callers expect confirmation that the update succeeded.
issues.suggestion: Check affected rows and return a boolean or throw: const result = await db.query(query, [completed, id]); if (result.rowCount === 0) { throw new Error(`Todo with id ${id} not found`); }

issues.description: deleteTodo() doesn't verify that the todo exists before deletion, silently succeeding even if the ID doesn't exist. This makes it impossible for callers to distinguish between successful deletion and deletion of non-existent items.
issues.suggestion: Check affected rows and return a boolean: const result = await db.query(query, [id]); if (result.rowCount === 0) { throw new Error(`Todo with id ${id} not found`); }

issues.description: Sanitization is applied before storage rather than at output time. This approach makes it impossible to change sanitization strategies later and stores pre-processed data instead of original user input.
issues.suggestion: Store raw validated data and sanitize at output/rendering time based on the output context (HTML, JSON, etc.). Remove lines 56-57 and sanitize when rendering to HTML.

issues.description: validateTodoInput() returns only a boolean without explaining which validation failed. This makes it difficult for API consumers to understand what's wrong with their input.
issues.suggestion: Return detailed validation errors: type ValidationResult = { valid: boolean; errors: string[] }; export function validateTodoInput(input: CreateTodoInput): ValidationResult { const errors: string[] = []; if (!input.title?.trim()) errors.push('Title is required'); if (input.title?.length > 200) errors.push('Title must be 200 characters or less'); if (input.description?.length > 1000) errors.push('Description must be 1000 characters or less'); return { valid: errors.length === 0, errors }; }

issues.description: searchTodosByStatus() accepts a string parameter 'completed' but should accept a boolean. The parameter type allows arbitrary strings to be passed, which combined with SQL injection makes this especially dangerous.
issues.suggestion: Change parameter type to boolean and use parameterized query: export async function searchTodosByStatus(completed: boolean): Promise<Todo[]> { const query = 'SELECT * FROM todos WHERE completed = $1'; const rows = await db.query(query, [completed]); return rows as Todo[]; }

codeQuality.summary: This file contains three critical SQL injection vulnerabilities (lines 123, 133, 143) that allow attackers to execute arbitrary SQL commands, along with weak cryptographic ID generation. While some functions use proper parameterized queries, the vulnerable search functions create severe security risks. Additional issues include missing error handling, lack of pagination, unsafe type assertions, and input sanitization applied at the wrong layer.

testCoverage.summary: No tests exist for src/todo.ts. The file contains 10 exported functions including 3 with critical SQL injection vulnerabilities (searchTodos, searchTodosByStatus, getTodosByUser). Security-critical functions like sanitizeInput and validateTodoInput are completely untested. The safe CRUD operations (createTodo, getAllTodos, getTodoById, updateTodoStatus, deleteTodo) also lack test coverage. Immediate priority is testing the vulnerable functions to demonstrate the security flaws, followed by comprehensive tests for validation, sanitization, and core business logic.

suggestions.description: Replace sequential if-return statements with early returns and combine validation logic to reduce nesting and improve readability.
suggestions.benefits: Uses optional chaining, reduces redundant checks, and caches trimmed value. More concise while maintaining clarity.

suggestions.description: Replace chained string.replace calls with a configuration-driven approach using reduce or a mapping object for better maintainability.
suggestions.benefits: Centralizes escape rules in a single map, makes it easier to add/remove entities, and reduces regex compilation overhead.

suggestions.description: Extract database query construction and execution into a separate function to separate concerns and improve testability.
suggestions.benefits: Separates validation, object construction, and persistence. Each function has a single responsibility and can be unit tested independently.

suggestions.description: Use optional chaining and nullish coalescing to simplify the conditional return logic.
suggestions.benefits: Eliminates unnecessary conditional and intermediate variable checks, making the code more concise while preserving behavior.

suggestions.description: Extract a TodoRepository class to encapsulate all database operations, applying dependency injection and separation of concerns.
suggestions.benefits: Centralizes all database logic, enables dependency injection for testing, makes it easier to swap database implementations, and groups related operations together.

suggestions.description: Use crypto.randomUUID() for more secure and standard-compliant ID generation instead of timestamp and random combination.
suggestions.benefits: Uses cryptographically secure UUID v4 standard, removes collision risk from timestamp-based IDs, and follows modern Node.js best practices.

refactorings.summary: The file has 8 refactoring opportunities ranging from modernizing syntax (optional chaining, nullish coalescing, crypto.randomUUID) to high-impact structural improvements (extracting a TodoRepository class, fixing SQL injection vulnerabilities). The most valuable changes are fixing the security vulnerabilities in search functions, introducing the repository pattern for better testability, and extracting the createTodo function into smaller, single-responsibility functions.

recommendations.description: Immediately fix SQL injection vulnerabilities in searchTodos(), searchTodosByStatus(), and getTodosByUser() by replacing string interpolation with parameterized queries. These vulnerabilities allow attackers to execute arbitrary SQL commands, potentially destroying data or exfiltrating sensitive information.

Create comprehensive security tests for the three vulnerable search functions to demonstrate the SQL injection exploits before fixing them, then verify the fixes prevent injection attacks. Test with payloads like "'; DROP TABLE todos; --" and "' OR '1'='1".
Implement tests for sanitizeInput() XSS prevention with malicious payloads like '<script>alert("xss")</script>' and verify all HTML special characters are properly escaped.
Replace weak ID generation (Math.random() and Date.now()) with cryptographically secure randomUUID() from the crypto module to prevent ID prediction attacks.

Create test suite covering all 10 exported functions. Current test coverage is 0%. Priority functions include validateTodoInput (boundary conditions), createTodo (validation failures, XSS handling), and all CRUD operations.
Add pagination to getAllTodos() to prevent memory exhaustion and DoS attacks when the todos table grows large. Implement LIMIT and OFFSET parameters with defaults (e.g., limit=100, offset=0).

Extract a TodoRepository class to encapsulate all database operations, enabling dependency injection, better testability, and separation of concerns. This refactoring will make it easier to swap database implementations and mock data access in tests.
Add error handling for database operations in all async functions. Wrap db.query() calls in try-catch blocks to provide meaningful error messages and prevent leaking database internals to clients.
Fix type safety issue in searchTodosByStatus() by changing the 'completed' parameter from string to boolean. Combined with SQL injection, this type mismatch is especially dangerous.

Refactor validateTodoInput() to return detailed validation errors instead of just boolean, helping API consumers understand what's wrong with their input. Return a ValidationResult type with { valid: boolean, errors: string[] }.

Move sanitization from storage time to output time. Currently sanitizeInput() is applied before storing data, which violates the principle of storing raw data and makes it impossible to change sanitization strategies later. Remove sanitization in createTodo() and apply it at rendering time.
Add runtime validation for database query results using libraries like zod or io-ts to catch type mismatches that TypeScript cannot detect at compile time.
